answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it earns influence, then weight votes by the locked amount and age rather than raw account count. Splitting one stake across many accounts creates no extra weight, while fake identities must tie up real capital and risk slashing if they misbehave. A ripple of linked accounts therefore cannot cheaply sway a summit; the attacker pays an opportunity cost for the whole voyage.
